display.title: The Three Weeks Begin: What Happened on the 17th of Tammuz
display.summary_short: Why there is no music during the Three Weeks, and the story of the siege of Yerushalayim, when the daily korban stopped on the 17th of Tammuz.
display.summary_long: A talk for Shiva Asar B'Tammuz from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that the Three Weeks begin today with a fast and end with Tisha B'Av, the saddest day of the year, and that we do not listen to music during these 21 days. Both the first and the second Beis HaMikdash were destroyed on Tisha B'Av. He traces the events of the year 3338: King Tzidkiyahu rebelled against Nevuchadnetzar of Bavel, whose army broke through the walls of Yerushalayim on the 9th of Tammuz. The Kohanim held out in the Beis HaMikdash, buying sheep for the daily korban tamid by lowering gold and silver over the wall, until on the 17th of Tammuz the soldiers kept the money and sent no sheep. For the first time in almost 900 years the daily offering stopped. Since baseless hatred caused the destruction, we must strengthen Ahavas Yisroel and say the Twelve Pesukim, so that Hashem will send Moshiach and turn these fast days into Yamim Tovim.
display.lesson: Learn from the past: the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred, so we must strengthen love and unity to bring the Geulah.
